texto_aprovado: And the treaty doesn't say how big a flood that is. No number, no line on a gauge. A flood on this river is measured in cubic feet per second: how much water goes past The Dalles every second. When the treaty came up for review, the two sides worked from different numbers. American planners projected that Canadian storage would come into play once the river's peak landed somewhere between 450,000 and 650,000. The Canadian side assumed it would be called only at 600,000, a flood expected to be rare. That's how the US Congressional Research Service describes those studies. Between 450,000 and 600,000, one side expects the call and the other doesn't. We'll call that the gap.
